For faraday.ca, tudorandcashel.com, carlowmayo.ca and limerick.ca, the non-www pages were blocked, so files came from the www. wp-content and wp-json endpoints. Everything else (verified_primary=false) rests on web-search summaries and may be stale. Key legal point confirmed in 316/03 s.4.1(2)-(3): in a municipality named in the 8/03 Table, ATVs, MOHUVs, ROVs, ETVs AND off-road motorcycles that meet Part III may use municipal roads without a by-law, but any by-law prohibition or limit still applies. Outside 8/03 (towns and cities such as Bancroft, Kawartha Lakes), ATV/UTV/ROV need a permitting by-law, and ETVs/dirt bikes need a by-law that specifically names them. 8/03 Table names checked for this area: listed are Addington Highlands, Admaston/Bromley, Algonquin Highlands, Asphodel-Norwood, Bonnechere Valley, Brudenell Lynoch and Raglan, Carlow/Mayo, Central Frontenac, Centre Hastings, Dysart et al, Faraday, Galway-Cavendish and Harvey (now Trent Lakes), Greater Madawaska, Hastings Highlands, Havelock-Belmont-Methuen, Highlands East, Killaloe Hagarty and Richards, Lake of Bays, Limerick, Madawaska Valley, Madoc, Marmora and Lake, Minden Hills, North Algona-Wilberforce, North Frontenac, North Kawartha, South Algonquin, Stirling-Rawdon, Tudor and Cashel, Tweed, Tyendinaga, Wollaston. NOT listed: Bancroft, Kawartha Lakes. Earlier caveat still stands: confirm current text before relying on anything marked low.

provincial.summary: Framework: HTA s.191.8 plus O. Reg. 316/03 (Operation of Off-Road Vehicles on Highways). s.2: no ORV on any highway except as the regulation permits, as Part IV permits, or as ORV Act cl. 2(2)(a) permits (direct crossing). s.3: no ORV on any highway in Schedule A ('highways prohibited to all off-road vehicles'). Schedule A covers the 400-series and QEW, plus named segments of King's highways (some found in the bbox are listed under highways). s.4: Schedule B highways are closed except to ATVs, two-up ATVs, ROVs, MOHUVs, ETVs and off-road motorcycles that meet Part III. MTO summary: permitted ORVs may use Highways 500-899, many 7000-series highways and some low-traffic highways, but not 400-series, the QEW or sections of the Trans-Canada. Part III conditions when on a highway: ride on the shoulder in the direction of traffic, as close to the right edge as practicable. Use the travelled lane only if the shoulder is unsafe, obstructed or too narrow to keep all tires off the roadway. Never ride in the median. Speed limits are 20 km/h where the posted limit is 50 km/h or less, and 50 km/h where it is over 50 km/h; a by-law may set a lower one. Driver must be 16+ with a G2/M2 or higher licence. Vehicle must have a permit, a rear plate and insurance, and the rider an approved helmet (seatbelts where fitted). Headlights and taillights stay on. A single-rider ATV may carry no passenger; on-road passengers on two-up machines must be 8+. Highways inside provincial parks are open only if the park permits ORVs (Algonquin does not). Municipal roads: an ORV may use a municipal highway only if a s.191.8(3) by-law permits it. Exception since Jan 1, 2021 (O. Reg. 740/20): in municipalities listed in O. Reg. 8/03 (former townships where the 80 km/h default applies), ORVs that meet 316/03 are allowed on municipal roads by default unless a by-law prohibits or restricts them. Elsewhere (towns, cities), no by-law means no on-road riding. Municipal by-laws may also limit months, hours, vehicle types, speeds and specific roads. Unverified: whether King's highways that are in neither Schedule A nor B are open by default. Sources disagree, so those are marked 'unknown'. Also unverified: whether a municipality can restrict ORVs on provincial highways inside its boundaries.
provincial.router_guidance: Suggested logic: (1) Never route along a Schedule A segment, which includes all 400-series. (2) Provincial 500-899 secondary highways still under MTO: shoulder allowed. (3) Former provincial highways now downloaded to counties or municipalities (e.g. 503, 507, 504, 620, 648, 121) follow the owning municipality's by-law, so check OSM operator/ref tags. (4) Other King's highways: treat as unknown/avoid unless verified. (5) Apply each municipality's rule to its own roads, and the county by-law to county roads.

provincial.crossing_rule: An ORV may be driven directly across a highway (Off-Road Vehicles Act cl. 2(2)(a), recognised in O. Reg. 316/03 s.2): the shortest route, at roughly a right angle, not travelling along it. On-road crossing conditions per OPP/MTO guidance: driver 16+ with G2/M2 or higher, vehicle registered with a rear plate and insured, helmet worn. Caveat: Schedule 1 of R.R.O. 1990 Reg. 863 (ORV Act) was replaced on Jan 1, 2021 by a reference to Schedule A of O. Reg. 316/03 (City of Hamilton memo, Dec 31, 2020). That suggests crossing may also be prohibited on Schedule A highways (e.g. Hwy 28 Apsley-Faraday, Hwy 62 Madoc-Bancroft, Hwy 118 Bracebridge-Haliburton) except perhaps at grade-separated or underpass crossings. Unverified: confirm before routing a crossing of a Schedule A segment. A by-law can also bar crossings of municipal roads or restrict them to set points.
provincial.o_reg_8_03_note: O. Reg. 8/03 lists local municipalities that were townships on Jan 1, 2003. Confirmed in its table from search snippets: Faraday, Hastings Highlands, Tudor and Cashel, Wollaston, Addington Highlands, Admaston/Bromley, Algonquin Highlands, Bonnechere Valley. Most other rural townships in the bbox are probably listed, but this is not verified. Towns and cities (Bancroft, Kawartha Lakes) are not. In listed municipalities with no by-law, compliant ORVs are allowed on municipal roads by default since Jan 1, 2021.

municipalities.name: Bancroft
municipalities.conditions: By-law 49-2015 (passed June 23, 2015; replaced the ATV-only 01-2004): 'Off-Road Vehicles shall be permitted on all roads and highways under the jurisdiction of the Town of Bancroft', covering ATVs incl. two-up, MOHUVs (UTVs) and ROVs (side-by-sides). Must meet O. Reg. 316/03 ss.7-15 equipment and ss.16-24 operating rules. Speed 20 km/h where posted 50 or less, 50 km/h where posted over 50. No season or hour limits in the text. By-law 43-2020 (Aug 11, 2020) amends 49-2015 by adding definitions of extreme terrain vehicles and off-road motorcycles; it adds no separate operative clause, but because 49-2015 permits 'Off-Road Vehicles' generally, the town treats ETVs and dirt bikes as included (local news reports council approving that). Hwy 28/62 in town are provincial, not covered by the by-law. Bancroft is a town and is NOT in O. Reg. 8/03, so only the by-law permits road riding. No newer ORV by-law found in Bancroft's 2021-2026 by-law folders.

Unopened road allowances need written council approval (By-law 21-2024, passed Apr 3, 2024). The township's site lists the PDF as 'ATV By-Law'.

Excluded: sidewalks and footpaths; municipal parks and beaches; private roads or driveways without the owner's consent; provincial highways; roads where passage is restricted under Municipal Act s.35; and unopened road allowances. No season, hour or township speed limits beyond the provincial ones. Repeals all earlier ORV by-laws. The Wollaston Rail Trail (township-owned multi-use trail) needs an OFATV, EOTA, KATVA or HATVA pass. Includes Coe Hill.

municipalities.conditions: County ORV By-law 3316/15, amended by 3326/16 and 3493/21: ORVs permitted on all County highways in Addington Highlands, Loyalist, Greater Napanee and Stone Mills EXCEPT the sections listed in Schedule A (restricted-sections map updated Nov 2022).

municipalities.name: County of Hastings (county roads)
municipalities.conditions: Hastings County appears to have no county road system: a 2020 Frontenac News column comparing counties says all comparators have county road systems 'except for Hastings County'. Numbered 'Hastings County Roads' (e.g. 62, 620) are owned by the lower tiers, so the router should apply the lower-tier municipality's rule. No county ORV by-law found. The county civicweb portal was reachable, but its search is JS-only and returned nothing usable.

municipalities.name: County of Frontenac
municipalities.conditions: Frontenac County is not known to own roads. The K&P Trail (County) allows ORVs with valid ORV Act permits under By-law 2022-0033; dirt bikes may be restricted (unverified forum claim).

permit_trail_systems.name: EOTA network incl. Hastings Heritage Trail (Glen Ross to Lake St. Peter, ~156 km, via Marmora, Bancroft)
permit_trail_systems.permit: EOTA trail pass ('OnePass'); Destination Ontario lists 'OnePass EOTA, OFATV'
permit_trail_systems.notes: Undated prices: about $150/yr, $75/week, $20/day; check current. Sold at Limerick Lake Lodge and 20+ outlets. EOTA's map has shown some trails its pass does not cover, which need an OFATV pass or no pass. The Park to Park trail joined the EOTA OnePass.

permit_trail_systems.name: Coe Hill Riders ATV Club (Wollaston Rail Trail, Limerick-area trails)
permit_trail_systems.permit: Trail access pass from OFATV, EOTA, KATVA or HATVA (Wollaston By-law 2021-0005); signs say a trail permit is required
permit_trail_systems.notes: Lease of the Wollaston Rail Trail extended to Feb 1, 2029 (2024 draft minutes). Limerick has club agreements (e.g. By-law 2025-04).

permit_trail_systems.name: HATVA - Haliburton ATV Association (1,700+ km) incl. Haliburton County Rail Trail
permit_trail_systems.permit: HATVA pass (KATVA pass also accepted on the Rail Trail)
permit_trail_systems.notes: Rail Trail motorized season May 1 - Nov 30. Lake of Bays ATV Club honours HATVA permits and sells day passes (~$20/day, $30/2 days).

permit_trail_systems.name: KATVA - Kawartha ATV Association (Kawartha Lakes / Victoria Rail Trail area)
permit_trail_systems.notes: Accepted on the Haliburton County Rail Trail.

permit_trail_systems.name: Renfrew County recreational trails (Algonquin Trail / Ottawa Valley Recreational Trail, K&P Trail in Renfrew County)
permit_trail_systems.permit: OFATV permit via getapermit.ofatv.org, choosing Renfrew County ATV Club (RCATV)
permit_trail_systems.notes: County By-law 139-24 (trail use; also 81-24). ATVs allowed May 1 - Nov 30. Older news saying ATVs ride free in Renfrew County is out of date.

permit_trail_systems.name: Haliburton Forest (private)
permit_trail_systems.permit: Haliburton Forest day/season permit (e.g. ~$52/day per driver + HST)
permit_trail_systems.notes: Private trail system, separate from HATVA.

permit_trail_systems.name: OFATV QuadON network (general)
permit_trail_systems.notes: Province-wide club network. Check which club covers which trail.

permit_trail_systems.name: Frontenac K&P Trail (Frontenac County)
permit_trail_systems.permit: Unclear; county by-law requires ORVs to hold valid ORV Act permits (vehicle permit). Whether a trail pass is required is unverified.

free_riding_notes: Municipal roads that a by-law opens (or 8/03 default-open) need no trail pass. The ORV still needs its plate, insurance, licence and helmet. Confirmed or likely all-road townships: Bancroft, Tudor and Cashel, Highlands East, Algonquin Highlands, Lake of Bays (except listed roads), Havelock-Belmont-Methuen (not Dec 1-Mar 31), North Kawartha (township roads).

Crown land: ORV use is generally allowed on Crown land and existing Crown roads and trails unless restricted by land-use planning, posted signs, or an MNRF road restriction or closure under the Public Lands Act. Building new trails or water crossings, or holding organised events, needs MNRF approval. Not allowed in provincial parks and some conservation reserves.

Provincial parks in or near the bbox (Algonquin, Silent Lake, Bon Echo, Kawartha Highlands Signature Site, Queen Elizabeth II Wildlands, Petroglyphs, etc.) do not permit ORVs except on roads or trails the park designates. Algonquin's Hwy 60 corridor is also Schedule A.
Unopened road allowances are not free riding: Faraday (By-law 21-2024), Tudor and Cashel (2023-34) and South Algonquin (2022-699) require written council approval; HBM prohibits ORVs on them.

Former rail trails owned by townships or counties (Wollaston Rail Trail, Haliburton County Rail Trail, Renfrew County Algonquin/K&P trails, Hastings Heritage Trail) all require a club or alliance pass. Do not route them as free.
North Frontenac historically sold its own permits for township roads and trails into Crown land and wilderness campsites (2008-09). Check current practice.

Forest access roads on Crown land (common north of Bancroft, in Hastings Highlands, South Algonquin, North Frontenac and Addington Highlands) are usually usable for free unless gated or posted. MNRF can restrict specific roads. Licensed forestry roads can be closed during operations.

For any 'unknown' municipality listed in O. Reg. 8/03, the 2021 default suggests its roads are open unless a by-law prohibits. Fewer than ten were actually confirmed in the 8/03 table, so keep these as low confidence.
